set: A: the site as web pages: the six pages at rest, the application with its controls on, the message page for touch devices, and the controls at their real size

issues.where: Step 3, between the assessment introduction and the mechanism on the right
issues.what: At rest the page introduces an assessment but gives no cue for how to start it or whether it is about to start automatically. The socket and tube look intentionally built into the page, but the empty work area makes the step look stalled.
issues.fix: Add a short, visible next-action or status line below the introduction. If the socket starts the assessment, label that interaction directly; if it starts automatically, show a ready or starting state.

issues.what: The message explains why the application is unavailable but offers no next action, even though the desktop experience provides a film alternative.
issues.fix: Give touch visitors a clearly labeled Watch the film action on the card and retain the desktop-device guidance as secondary copy.

issues.where: Submit button near the bottom center
issues.what: The action is detached from the verification card by a large gap and breaks the right-aligned action pattern of the previous steps. Its active orange treatment also competes with the unchecked prerequisite.
issues.fix: Use a shared action row with a consistent right alignment and a tighter relationship to the verification block. Make it clear whether Submit is available before verification.

issues.where: Contact number, date of birth, and audio volume controls
issues.what: All three controls look like the same empty dropdown. There is no visible format cue for the first two or current value for the volume, so the visitor cannot predict what opening each one will do.
issues.fix: Show a format cue or current value in each resting field. Preserve the misleading mechanism reveal if it is part of the joke, but start from a believable control state.

issues.where: Live utility row above the application header, Skip step link
issues.what: The utility row is quiet and legible, but Accept Defeat makes the real escape control sound like another part of the joke.
issues.fix: Keep the utility row understated and label the real escape simply Skip this step.
